new_quiz.q: What is a specialization on this site?
choices: A badge you get for finishing a quest
A setting that changes the colours of your player card
The area of Unreal Engine you want to focus on
A group of members who work on one project
new_quiz.explain: A specialization is the area of Unreal Engine you want to focus on, such as level design or programming. It tells the site what you want to learn.

new_quiz.q: What does your primary specialization decide?
choices: Which quests your path shows you first
Which version of Unreal Engine you must install
How many questions each quiz has
Who is allowed to see your player card
new_quiz.explain: The primary specialization sets the order of your path, so the quests for that area come first. It does not lock you out of anything.

new_quiz.q: Where do you pick your primary specialization?
choices: On the Achievements page, under Unlocked
On the Quest Board, in the part named My path
In the chest at the bottom of a quest page
On your player card page, under Specializations
new_quiz.explain: You open your player card page, press Change under Specializations, pick a primary specialization and press Save.

new_quiz.q: You are not sure yet which area you like most. What can you do?
choices: Wait, because the first choice can never be changed
Choose Undecided, and change your choice later
Skip the choice, because it has no effect on your path
Pick every specialization as primary at the same time
new_quiz.explain: It is fine to choose Undecided. You can change your primary specialization at any time, so there is no wrong answer.

new_quiz.q: What happens if you later become interested in a second area?
choices: You must start again with a new account
You lose the quests you already finished
You can add more specializations to the one you have
You must ask a mentor to unlock that area
new_quiz.explain: You can add more specializations later and keep your primary one. The choice only guides your path, it does not close the other areas.

new_quiz.q: Which three pages of the site will you come back to often?
choices: Your player card, the Quest Board and Achievements
The Quest Board, the chest and the settings page
Your player card, the motto page and the path page
Achievements, the review page and the help page
new_quiz.explain: The player card shows who you are, the Quest Board lists the quests, and Achievements shows what you have unlocked.

new_quiz.q: How do you open your player card?
choices: Press Send in the chest of any quest
Open the Quest Board and click My path
Open Achievements and click the first item
Click your name at the top right of the page
new_quiz.explain: Your name at the top right of the page is the link to your player card. From the card you can also reach Achievements.

new_quiz.q: What does the part named My path on the Quest Board show?
choices: Every quest on the site in order of its id
The quests you should do next
The quests that other members finished today
Only the quests you have already finished
new_quiz.explain: My path always shows what you should do next, so you do not have to search the whole list of quests.

new_quiz.q: What does your player card show?
choices: The steps of the quest you are doing now
The list of all Epic documentation pages
Who you are and how far you have come
The questions of the next quiz
new_quiz.explain: The player card is your own page. It shows who you are and your progress.

new_quiz.q: From which page do you open Achievements in this quest?
choices: From the Quest Board
From your player card page
From the chest on a quest page
From the part named My path
new_quiz.explain: You go back to your player card page and open Achievements from there. Achievements shows what you have unlocked.

new_quiz.q: What is your player card?
choices: A list of the quests you should do next
The place where you send proof of your work
A page that only mentors can open
The page that other members see when they look at you
new_quiz.explain: The player card is your public page on the site. Other members see it when they look at you, which is why it is worth making it yours.

new_quiz.q: What is a motto on your player card?
choices: A picture that frames your name
One short line of text about you
The name of your primary specialization
A title you unlock with a quest
new_quiz.explain: A motto is one line of text about you. Writing it is the first small change you make to your card.

new_quiz.q: Which button do you press on your player card page to write a motto?
choices: Edit profile
Change
Send
My path
new_quiz.explain: You press Edit profile, write a short motto, and then press Save. Change is the button for specializations.

new_quiz.q: How do more colours, frames and titles become available for your card?
choices: You pick a second specialization
You open the Achievements page once
You finish quests
You write a longer motto
new_quiz.explain: More ways to change the look of your card unlock as you finish quests. The motto is available from the start.

new_quiz.q: You wrote a motto but the quest is still not complete. What do you check first?
choices: That you sent a screenshot of the card
That you opened the Quest Board afterwards
That you picked a new colour and frame
That you pressed Save after writing it
new_quiz.explain: The quest is complete as soon as a motto is saved on your player card. Text that you typed but did not save does not count, and nothing has to be sent.

new_quiz.q: What is the chest on a quest page?
choices: The list of steps of the quest
The place where you send your work
The quiz at the end of the quest
The link to the Epic documentation
new_quiz.explain: On the quest page, the place where you send your work is called the chest. You type or attach your proof there and press Send.

new_quiz.q: How do most quests end?
choices: You wait one day before the next quest opens
You install a new version of Unreal Engine
You change your primary specialization
You send proof of your work
new_quiz.explain: Most quests end with you sending proof, such as a screenshot or a few lines of text. The proof shows that you did the steps.

new_quiz.q: What do you send in this practice quest?
choices: The word READY
A screenshot of your player card
A short video of the editor
A link to your project files
new_quiz.explain: You type the single word READY into the chest and press Send. The goal is only to try the chest once.

new_quiz.q: Why do you practice sending work with a single word?
choices: Because the chest only accepts short words
Because a mentor must check your spelling
So you know how it works before a real quest asks for it
So your player card gets a new frame
new_quiz.explain: The practice removes the surprise later. When a real quest asks for proof, you already know where the chest is and how to use it.

new_quiz.q: Which of these is a normal kind of proof for a quest?
choices: Your password for the site
A screenshot or a few lines of text
The motto from your player card
The name of your computer
new_quiz.explain: Proof of work is usually a screenshot or a few lines of text. Each quest says which kind it needs.

new_quiz.q: In the level editor, what does the G key do?
choices: It groups the selected actors
It turns the grid snapping off
It switches game view on and off
It starts Play in Editor
new_quiz.explain: G switches game view on and off. Game view shows the level the way it looks in the game, without the editor icons.

new_quiz.q: You selected an actor in the level and want to find its asset in the Content Browser. Which shortcut do you press?
choices: Ctrl+B
Ctrl+H
Alt+B
new_quiz.explain: Ctrl+B finds the selected asset in the Content Browser. It saves you from searching through folders by hand.

new_quiz.q: What happens when you hold Alt and drag an actor in the viewport?
choices: The actor is hidden
The actor snaps to the floor
The camera orbits around the actor
A copy of the actor is made
new_quiz.explain: Alt+drag makes a copy of the actor and moves the copy. It is a quick way to repeat walls, props and lights.

new_quiz.q: You pressed H and the selected actor is no longer visible. How do you show hidden actors again?
choices: Press G
Press Ctrl+H
Press F11
Press Ctrl+B
new_quiz.explain: H hides the selected actor, and Ctrl+H shows hidden actors again. The actor was not deleted, only hidden in the editor.

new_quiz.q: Which key makes the viewport fullscreen?
choices: F8
G
H
new_quiz.explain: F11 makes the viewport fullscreen, and pressing it again brings the other panels back.

new_quiz.q: Why must the text in an editor screenshot be easy to read?
choices: Because the site rejects pictures with small text
Because mentors can only review what they can read
Because small text makes the image file too large
Because Unreal Engine cannot save small text
new_quiz.explain: A screenshot of a graph or a Details panel is not useful if nobody can read it. Many people also look at it on a phone, where text gets even smaller.

new_quiz.q: Where do you open the High Resolution Screenshot tool?
choices: In the Content Browser, under Add
In the Details panel, under Rendering
In the Outliner, under Settings
In Viewport Options, the menu button in the top left corner of the viewport
new_quiz.explain: You click Viewport Options in the top left corner of the viewport and choose High Resolution Screenshot.

new_quiz.q: What does the High Resolution Screenshot tool do?
choices: It takes a picture of the viewport at a higher resolution than your screen
It records a video of the game while it runs
It takes a picture of the whole editor with all panels
It sends a picture of the viewport to a mentor
new_quiz.explain: The tool captures the viewport at a higher resolution than your screen, so the picture stays sharp when someone zooms in.

new_quiz.q: Which test tells you that your screenshot of a Blueprint graph is good enough to send?
choices: The whole graph fits in one picture
The picture shows your desktop and taskbar
The text can still be read at the size of a phone screen
The picture file is as small as possible
new_quiz.explain: The picture must stay readable on a small screen. If the node names are too small on a phone, zoom in and show a smaller part of the graph.

new_quiz.q: A mentor says the node names in your graph screenshot cannot be read. What do you do first?
choices: Send the same picture again as a video
Zoom in on the important part and take the screenshot again
Add a long text that lists every node
Take a photo of your monitor with a phone
new_quiz.explain: The fix is to make the text larger in the picture. Zoom in on the part that matters so the graph or the Details panel is easy to read.

new_quiz.q: What does PIE mean in Unreal Engine?
choices: Project Import and Export
Preview in Explorer
Picture in Editor
Play in Editor
new_quiz.explain: PIE means Play in Editor. It is the game running inside the editor after you press Play.

new_quiz.q: When is a short video clip a better proof than a screenshot?
choices: When you show something that moves, such as a door that opens
When you show the settings in a Details panel
When you show the folders in the Content Browser
When you show the names of nodes in a graph
new_quiz.explain: Movement cannot be shown in a still picture. A door that opens or a character that moves needs a clip.

new_quiz.q: After you record your clip, why do you trim it?
choices: So the clip plays at a higher resolution
So the editor can open the clip again
So only the useful part is left
So the sound is removed from the clip
new_quiz.explain: Trimming cuts away the start and the end where nothing happens. The person who reviews the clip then sees only the important part.

new_quiz.q: Which file types can you send your clip as?
choices: PNG, JPG or GIF
MP4, WebM or MOV
ZIP, RAR or 7Z
UASSET, UMAP or UPROJECT
new_quiz.explain: The clip must be a video file: MP4, WebM or MOV. Picture files and project files are not accepted as a clip.

new_quiz.q: How long may the clip be when you send it?
choices: Shorter than 20 seconds
Exactly one minute
At least two minutes
Any length, if it is trimmed
new_quiz.explain: You record 10 to 20 seconds and the clip you send must be shorter than 20 seconds. A short clip is quick to watch and review.

new_quiz.q: Which four parts does a good help post have?
choices: Your name, your country, your age and your computer
A greeting, an apology, a thank you and a deadline
What you want to happen, what happens instead, what you tried, and your engine version
The project name, the level name, the asset name and the folder name
new_quiz.explain: These four parts give a helper everything needed to find the cause. Without them the helper must ask questions before any answer is possible.

new_quiz.q: Why is the post "my door doesnt work pls help" a bad help post?
choices: It is written without capital letters
It does not say what should happen, what happens instead, or what was tried
It is about a door, which is too simple a topic
It is too short to be shown on the page
new_quiz.explain: The post gives no details, so nobody can tell what the problem is. An unclear question often gets no answer.

new_quiz.q: Why do you write which engine version you use?
choices: Because helpers only answer users of the newest version
Because the version changes the price of the engine
Because the site sorts posts by version number
Because menus and features differ between versions
new_quiz.explain: The right answer can depend on the version, since tools and menus change. With the version in the post, the helper can give steps that fit your editor.

new_quiz.q: Why do you list what you already tried?
choices: So helpers do not suggest things you have already done
So the post becomes long enough to be accepted
So helpers can see how many hours you worked
So the post is moved to the top of the list
new_quiz.explain: What you tried rules out some causes and saves time for everyone. The helper can go straight to ideas that are new to you.

new_quiz.q: Which sentence is the best start for the rewritten door post?
choices: My door is broken and I need help fast.
Doors in Unreal Engine never work for me.
I want my door Blueprint to open when the player walks up to it, but it stays closed.
Can someone send me a door Blueprint that works?
new_quiz.explain: This sentence says what you want to happen and what happens instead. Those are the first two parts of a good help post.

new_quiz.q: Which three things does a good review name?
choices: Three problems, sorted from large to small
A score, a rank and a final grade
The tools, the time and the cost of the work
One thing that works, one specific issue and one next step
new_quiz.explain: Good feedback says what works, what the problem is, and what to do next. The person then knows what to keep and what to change.

new_quiz.q: Which of these is specific feedback?
choices: The level feels a bit off.
The exit door is hard to see because it has the same colour as the wall.
The lighting could be better.
Nice work, keep going.
new_quiz.explain: Specific feedback names the exact thing and the reason. The other sentences do not tell the person what to look at or what to change.

new_quiz.q: How does reviewing the work of other people help you?
choices: It teaches you to look at your own work more clearly
It lets you copy their project files
It removes the need to send your own work
It makes your own screenshots sharper
new_quiz.explain: Giving feedback is a skill you can practice. When you learn to see what works and what does not in other work, you see the same things in your own.

new_quiz.q: You have no work from another learner at hand. What can you review instead?
choices: Your own player card
A page of the Epic documentation
The sample level of a project made from the Third Person template
A level from a game that you bought
new_quiz.explain: You open a project made from the Third Person template and review its sample level as if another learner had built it.

new_quiz.q: Why does a review end with a next step?
choices: So the review reaches the minimum length
So the person knows what to do after reading it
So the reviewer can show more knowledge
So the person must send the work again
new_quiz.explain: Naming a problem is only half of the help. A next step turns the feedback into something the person can act on.

new_quiz.q: What does WIP mean?
choices: Work in progress
World in preview
Window in panel
Work is perfect
new_quiz.explain: WIP means work in progress, which is work that is not finished yet. Showing it early lets you fix problems while they are still small.

new_quiz.q: Why do you ask one specific question when you show your work?
choices: So people answer with only yes or no
So people cannot say anything negative
So people know what kind of feedback you want
So people do not look at the rest of the work
new_quiz.explain: A specific question points people at the part you are unsure about. The feedback you get is then easier to use.

new_quiz.q: Why is it useful to show work that is not finished?
choices: Unfinished work cannot be criticised
Finished work may not be shown to other people
Other people will finish the work for you
Hearing what is wrong with it is how you get better quickly
new_quiz.explain: Early critique shows problems before you have spent many hours on them. That is the fastest way to improve.

new_quiz.q: What must your reply to the feedback say?
choices: That the feedback was wrong
What you will change, or why you will not change it
That you will start the work again from zero
How long you worked on the piece
new_quiz.explain: A good reply shows that you thought about the feedback. You either say what you will change, or give your reason for keeping it as it is.

new_quiz.q: Which three things do you send as proof?
choices: A screenshot, a clip and a project file
The question you asked, the feedback you got and your reply
Your name, your motto and your specialization
Three different works in progress
new_quiz.explain: You send the question, the feedback and your reply as text. Together they show the whole exchange.
